note: Places for towns and cities of today. `water` only where the place has that water.

places.summary: A bright corner coffee shop with a long communal table, oat milk everything and laptops by nine.
A bakery cafe with sourdough out at seven, cardamom buns gone by ten and a queue on Saturdays.
A worn-in coffee shop with mismatched armchairs, a book swap shelf and the same barista for nine years.
A roastery with the roaster running in the window, pour-overs and a barista who will talk beans for an hour.
A tea shop with forty loose teas in tins, scones and a quiet back room where people actually read.
A chrome diner with booths, bottomless coffee, pancakes all day and pie in a rotating case.
Hand-rolled bagels, a dozen schmears and a line out the door before the commuter train.
A cafe inside a second-hand bookshop, where you can read anything on the shelves as long as you buy a drink.
Bubble tea in every colour, toast boxes and a crowd of students after school.
A cafe on the waterfront with chowder, coffee and a deck over the water where gulls try to steal your fries.
A family-run Italian place with hand-made pasta, a wood oven and the owner's mother checking every plate.
A taqueria with al pastor turning on the spit, a salsa bar and tacos three for nine dollars.
A big Cantonese restaurant with round tables, dim sum carts on weekends and roast duck in the window.
A narrow ramen bar of twelve stools, rich tonkotsu, a forty-minute wait and no reservations.
A quiet sushi counter where the chef serves omakase and remembers what you didn't like last time.
Big bowls of pho, banh mi and iced coffee with condensed milk, fast and cheap and always busy at lunch.
Tandoori from the clay oven, a long lunch buffet and a lamb vindaloo that comes with a warning.
A Thai place with green curry, papaya salad at whatever heat you dare and a fish tank by the door.
A steakhouse with leather booths, dry-aged steaks, martinis and a waiter who has been there since it opened.
A farm-to-table bistro with a chalkboard menu, a natural wine list and a kitchen open to the room.
Pizza by the slice, a jukebox and booths carved with forty years of initials.
Lobster rolls, fried clams and chowder at picnic tables by the water, cash only and worth the line.
An oyster bar with a dozen kinds on ice, crudo, fried fish and a big window onto the harbor.
Lebanese grill with charcoal kebabs, mezze for the table, warm pita and baklava that goes fast.
Korean barbecue with grills in every table, banchan that keeps coming and a crowd celebrating something.
Brisket and ribs smoked overnight, sold by the pound until it runs out, with banana pudding and sweet tea.
A weekend brunch place with a two-hour wait, shakshuka, chicken and waffles and mimosas by the carafe.
A tiny French bistro of steak frites, onion soup, a zinc bar and candles in wine bottles.
A converted warehouse of food stalls: dumplings, tacos, poke, a bar in the middle and long shared tables.
A plant-based place with grain bowls, cashew cheese and a carrot cake people cross town for.
Shared platters on injera, eaten with your hands, and a coffee ceremony on Sunday afternoons.
A neighbourhood pub with twenty taps, a dartboard, trivia on Tuesday and a bartender who knows your order.
A brewery taproom in an old garage, a food truck out front, dogs under the tables and a new IPA every week.
A dim cocktail bar with a leather menu, bartenders in waistcoats and drinks with three-word names.
A dive bar with a pool table, cheap pitchers, a jukebox that only plays the seventies and a cat.
A narrow wine bar with natural wines by the glass, small plates and a sommelier who won't let you pick badly.
A rooftop bar with string lights, frozen drinks and a sunset view that fills it every summer evening.
Thirty screens, wings by the dozen and the whole town in jerseys when the team plays.
A bar on the dock with picnic tables, boats tied up alongside and live music on summer weekends.
A bar with a wall of five hundred board games and a staff who will teach you any of them.
Private rooms, a main stage on Friday and regulars who only ever sing the same power ballad.
A club in an old warehouse with a big sound system, DJs from out of town and a crowd until four.
A basement jazz club with a house trio, a two-drink minimum and a Monday jam that runs late.
Stand-up most nights, open mic on Wednesday and a front row nobody wants to sit in.
Salsa and bachata nights with a lesson at eight and a packed floor by ten.
A queer bar with drag shows on Thursday, a dance floor at weekends and the friendliest door staff in town.
A restored old theater with touring musicals, a classic film series and a lobby full of red velvet.
A mid-size concert hall for touring bands, a standing floor and a balcony with the best sightlines.
An independent cinema with three screens, arthouse films, a bar in the lobby and real butter on the popcorn.
A community theater in a converted church putting on four plays a year with whoever turns up to audition.
An outdoor amphitheater with lawn seats, summer concerts and fireworks on the Fourth.
Twenty-four lanes, cosmic bowling on Friday nights, a league on Tuesdays and a snack bar with great fries.
Old arcade cabinets and pinball machines lined up beside a bar, tokens a quarter each.
An art museum with a modern wing, a sculpture court and free admission on Thursday evenings.
A local history museum in an old mansion, with a room of old signs and a guide who loves the town.
A hands-on science museum with a planetarium, a tornado machine and school groups every weekday morning.
Ship models, a walk-through lighthouse lens and an old fishing schooner tied up outside.
A children's museum of water tables, a pretend grocery and a climbing structure two storeys high.
The public library with a quiet reading room, a maker space, free wifi and story time on Saturday.
A big campus library with study carrels, a twenty-four hour floor in exam season and rare books upstairs.
A big town park with a lake, tennis courts, a dog run and a summer concert series at the bandshell.
A paved riverwalk with benches, a playground and kayak rentals by the footbridge.
A waterfront park on old pier land with lawns, a splash pad and the best sunset in town.
The town green with a gazebo, a farmers' market on Saturdays and the Christmas tree in December.
A fenced dog park with a small-dog side, a water fountain and a regular crowd who know every dog's name.
A concrete skate park with a bowl, rails and teenagers who are much better than you.
Big outdoor sculptures scattered across a hillside meadow, free to wander and full of picnics in summer.
A botanical garden with a glass conservatory, a Japanese garden and a lantern festival every winter.
A community garden on a vacant lot, with raised beds, a beehive and a potluck at harvest.
A rose garden on a terrace, popular for wedding photos and quiet lunch breaks.
A sandy town beach with a lifeguard stand, a snack shack and volleyball nets in summer.
A small rocky cove with tide pools, reached by a steep path the tourists don't know about.
A surf beach with a break that works at mid-tide, a surf school van and wetsuits drying on fences.
An old railway line turned into a paved trail for walkers, runners and cyclists, out through the woods to the next town.
A hiking trail up through oak and pine to a rocky summit with a view over the whole town.
A flat loop around the lake, popular with joggers at dawn and strollers in the evening.
A path along the bluffs above the sea, with benches, wildflowers and the odd seal on the rocks.
A nature preserve of boardwalks over wetland, bird blinds and a visitor center with a stuffed owl.
A twenty-four hour gym with a crowded squat rack at six, spin classes and a smoothie bar.
A sunlit yoga studio above the shops, hot yoga in the mornings and gentle flow on Sunday.
A bouldering gym in an old factory with routes reset every week and a cafe up on the mezzanine.
A community rec center with a pool, a basketball court, pickleball and classes for every age.
A boxing gym with a ring, heavy bags and a coach who trains pros and beginners side by side.
A rowing and kayak club with dawn practice, rentals by the hour and a deck for after.
The minor league ballpark with cheap seats, fireworks Fridays and a mascot nobody can name.
An arena for the hockey team, concerts and the high school graduation.
A Saturday farmers' market of produce, cheese, flowers, a kettle corn stand and a busker with a banjo.
A member-owned grocery co-op with bulk bins, local bread and a notice board for everything in town.
A summer night market of food stalls, string lights, local makers and a DJ in the parking lot.
A fish market on the pier selling the day's catch straight off the boats.
A big international grocery with a hot food counter, fifty kinds of noodles and a bakery by the door.
An independent bookstore with staff picks on every shelf, author readings and a shop cat.
Crates of vinyl, a listening station and a clerk who will judge your taste only a little.
Vintage clothes, mid-century lamps and a rack of fifty-dollar leather jackets that sell in a day.
An indoor mall with a food court, a cinema, the usual chains and teenagers doing laps.
A strip of local shops: a hardware store, a florist, a toy shop and a cheese shop that gives samples.
Comics, tabletop games and a back room with Friday night card tournaments.
A charity thrift store where half price day brings out every collector in town.
An aquarium with a touch tank, a shark tunnel and harbor seals fed at eleven and three.
A small zoo with red pandas, a reptile house, a carousel and a train round the grounds.
Old-fashioned rides, a Ferris wheel, skee-ball and fried dough, open all summer.
Four themed escape rooms, from a submarine to a haunted library, sixty minutes to get out.
A vineyard tasting room with a patio, flights of local wine and live music on Sunday afternoons.
A white lighthouse on the point, open for tours on summer weekends, with the whole coast from the top.
A domed old courthouse on the square, lit up at night, with a clock that is usually four minutes slow.
An old iron bridge turned footbridge, covered in love locks and the best photo spot in town.
A lookout on the hill road with a parking pull-off, coin binoculars and the whole valley below.
A block of brick walls painted by local artists, repainted every summer at a street festival.
A marina of sailboats and cruisers, a fuel dock, a chandlery and a harbor master's hut.
The ferry landing with a ticket hut, a coffee cart and boats out to the islands every hour.
The working fish pier, lobster traps stacked high and boats unloading in the afternoon.
An old stone church with a bell tower, a choir that welcomes anyone and a soup kitchen in the basement.
A mosque and community center with Friday prayers, an iftar dinner open to everyone in Ramadan and a weekend school.
A synagogue with a busy calendar of classes, a book club and a Purim party the whole town hears.
A quiet meditation center in an old house, with morning sits, a tea garden and a strict no-phones rule.
A busy vet clinic with a waiting room of nervous dogs, a resident cat and a Saturday walk-in hour.
A small vet practice that knows every pet in the neighbourhood by name.
